problem: 2D semantic-map/frontier methods lack object relations and long-term memory, while scene-graph memories are discrete and give no exploration guidance in continuous space, so no single representation supports memory, exploration and online updates together.
motivation: Humans combine explicit memory (recalling seen objects) with implicit spatial intuition (which direction likely leads to the goal). Lifelong multimodal navigation with category, language and image goals needs a persistent, reusable memory plus goal-conditioned exploration guidance, ideally usable with small on-device VLMs.
key_idea: Couple a persistent multimodal scene graph (explicit memory) with a goal-conditioned semantic-frontier field projected from the same graph (implicit intuition), inside a training-free VLM navigation loop with verification feedback.
insight: Deriving the exploration field from the graph lets one shared representation drive retrieval, subgraph selection and frontier choice. With the same Qwen3-VL-8B backbone, this raises overall SR from 53.2 to 63.0 and SPL from 30.0 to 39.6 over MSGNav, and even beats MSGNav with GPT-4o overall, so a better representation compensates for a weaker VLM. Image-goal gains are smaller (53.4 SR vs 59.1 for GPT-4o MSGNav), suggesting image goals depend more on fine-grained visual correspondence than on exploration. No component ablations are reported.
method: Multimodal scene graph: following MSGNav, YOLOv8-World + SAM + CLIP build nodes (category, 3D position, feature, images) with relation edges; nodes are augmented with goal-conditioned verification statistics (count, goal, outcome, multiview feedback).

Semantic field: each node's CLIP goal-relevance (minus a background baseline, gated by a verification mask) is a point source diffused over observed free space with exponential geodesic decay and a cutoff. The top-K_s sources are summed per cell, and updates are local around changed objects.

Frontier scoring: frontiers are scored by the mean field value in a traversable neighbourhood, discounted by geodesic distance. If the best score is below a threshold, the agent falls back to the nearest frontier.

Semantic-guided subgraph selection: replaces MSGNav's KSS object-selection stage. Positive-relevance nodes plus one-hop neighbours form a seed set, and a VLM selects extra nodes from a compressed residual graph. MSGNav's edge pruning and image allocation are kept.
VLM reasoning with decision memory: the VLM takes the goal, key subgraph and a compressed decision log, then outputs an object target, an image target or an Explore request.

Action selection: an object node's position is used directly, and an image candidate is re-detected. Explore goes to the best-scoring frontier, else to the centroid of the semantic peak, else the subtask fails.

Verification and closed loop: the VLM returns Yes / No-Uncertain / No-Confirmed from viewpoints. Rejected nodes are suppressed in the field for the rest of the subtask, not deleted. Graph is kept across subtasks, field rebuilt per goal, decision memory reset.

setting.action_space: high-level destinations (object node / image target / frontier) executed by a low-level planner

numbers.eval_set_note: first episode of each of the 36 scenes: 36 episodes, 278 subtasks
numbers.extra: training-free; 0.25 m success threshold as stated in the paper
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Navigation performance across the first episode of each scene on the Val Unseen split of GOAT-Bench; CGFM-Nav (Qwen3VL-8B) row

results: On a 36-episode subset of GOAT-Bench val-unseen, CGFM-Nav with Qwen3-VL-8B reaches 63.0 SR / 39.6 SPL, versus 53.2 / 30.0 for MSGNav with the same backbone. It also beats MSGNav with GPT-4o (60.0 / 37.0) overall, on category and on language goals, but not on image goals (59.1 SR, 42.6 SPL for GPT-4o MSGNav).
limitations: Evaluated only on a small subset of GOAT-Bench (first episode per scene, 36 episodes), with no ablations of graph vs field components.
Image-goal navigation still trails MSGNav with GPT-4o and depends on fine-grained visual correspondence.
No real-robot validation and no other benchmarks yet (both left as future work).
